title: Promised short-path s–t connectivity

problem.name: Promised short-path $s$–$t$ connectivity
problem.statement_latex:
Given an undirected graph and vertices $s,t$, distinguish the existence of an $s$--$t$ path of length at most $d$ from complete disconnection. The positive-instance path-length promise exposes how certificate structure affects quantum complexity.
The comparison counts adjacency-matrix queries and the quantum working space used between queries.
problem.statement_text: Given an undirected graph and vertices $s,t$, distinguish the existence of an $s$–$t$ path of length at most $d$ from complete disconnection. The positive-instance path-length promise exposes how certificate structure affects quantum complexity. The comparison counts adjacency-matrix queries and the quantum working space used between queries.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(n\sqrt d)$ queries and $\widetilde O(n\sqrt d)$ time, Belovs--Reichardt span-program connectivity.
quantum.headline_text: $O(n\sqrt d)$ queries and $\widetilde O(n\sqrt d)$ time, Belovs–Reichardt span-program connectivity.
quantum.details_latex: The promise is that connected terminals have a path of at most $d$ edges. The algorithm uses logarithmic quantum space. The case $d=\Theta(n)$ gives $O(n^{3/2})$ queries. For very small $d$, direct specialized tests can improve the displayed general upper bound; for $d=1$ a single adjacency query suffices.
quantum.details_text: The promise is that connected terminals have a path of at most $d$ edges. The algorithm uses logarithmic quantum space. The case $d=\Theta(n)$ gives $O(n^{3/2})$ queries. For very small $d$, direct specialized tests can improve the displayed general upper bound; for $d=1$ a single adjacency query suffices.

classical.headline_latex: $O(n^2)$ matrix time and queries, breadth-first search; $O(n+m)$ with explicit adjacency lists.
classical.headline_text: $O(n^2)$ matrix time and queries, breadth-first search; $O(n+m)$ with explicit adjacency lists.
classical.details_latex: The unrestricted matrix-oracle problem has classical complexity $\Theta(n^2)$. The promise parameter must be retained when comparing algorithms on shorter-path subclasses. A classical traversal records discovered vertices and stops once $t$ is reached or its component has been exhausted.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial oracle speedup, including $n^2\to n^{3/2}$ for the unrestricted path-length regime. The mechanism is a span program and quantum reflections.
strength.description_text: Polynomial oracle speedup, including $n^2\to n^{3/2}$ for the unrestricted path-length regime. The mechanism is a span program and quantum reflections.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous query advantage in the regime where the classical quadratic lower bound applies.
evidence.description_text: Rigorous query advantage in the regime where the classical quadratic lower bound applies.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm uses $O(\log n)$ logical working qubits up to precision ancillas, with coherent adjacency access. This space-efficient construction still needs fault tolerance for its long sequence of queries.
